questions.question: Several workers poll a jobs table and must never pick the same job, without waiting on each other. Which query fits best?
options: SELECT ... LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
questions.explanation: SKIP LOCKED skips rows already locked by other workers, so each worker claims a different job immediately. NOWAIT would just raise an error.

questions.question: Under REPEATABLE READ, why can `UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE coupon_code = 'DIWALI50'` block almost all other writes when coupon_code is unindexed?
options: MySQL escalates row locks to a table lock after 1,000 rows
UPDATE always takes a table-level metadata write lock
InnoDB scans the clustered index and sets next-key locks on every row it examines, not just the matches
Unindexed columns are stored in a separate locked page
questions.explanation: InnoDB locks index records it scans. Without an index the whole clustered index is scanned and locked; InnoDB does not do lock escalation.

questions.question: What does a gap lock block?
options: Inserts into the gap between index records
All reads of the neighbouring rows
Other gap locks on the same gap
questions.explanation: Gap locks exist to prevent inserts (and so phantoms); they are compatible with each other and do not block MVCC reads.

questions.question: Your application receives ERROR 1213 (Deadlock found when trying to get lock). What is the correct response?
options: Retry only the last statement that failed
Retry the entire transaction (bounded, with backoff), and fix lock ordering if it recurs
questions.explanation: InnoDB rolls back the whole victim transaction on a deadlock, so the full transaction must be rerun. Consistent lock ordering reduces how often it happens.
